## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Ussayavādikā* ("The training rule on taking legal action") is the first rule in the *saṅghādisesa* category of the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* in the Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule stipulates that a nun who engages in inappropriate or contentious legal action against another party is subject to suspension, requiring formal meetings of the Community (*saṅghādisesa*) for rehabilitation. An English translation of the rule and its associated analysis is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Within the Pali canon, it corresponds to the first *saṅghādisesa* in the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (*pli-tv-bi-pm-ss1*) and the *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (*Saṅghādisesa 1*). Across other Vinaya lineages, parallel rules are preserved in Chinese translations of the Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Ss 4* and its *pātimokkha*), Mahīśāsaka (*Lzh Mi Bi Vb Ss 7*), Sarvāstivāda (*Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Ss 7*), and Mahāsaṅghika (*Lzh Mg Bi Vb Ss 4*), as well as in Sanskrit versions of the Lokottaravāda (*san-lo-bi-vb-ss4*) and Sarvāstivāda (*san-sarv-bi-vb-ss7*) traditions.
